title: Ben Netzer
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman cites Ketubot 51a for the report that he was a bandit who conquered towns and ruled them. At the end of Terumot chapter 8, Hyman says Queen Zenobia told Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Shmuel, “With this sword Bar Netzer killed,” etc. See Bereshit Rabbah 76:6.

notes.text: The consulted Terumot paragraph has an entering Saracen say that Bar Netzer killed his brother with this sword. Hyman instead assigns the abbreviated statement to Zenobia. The source’s active “killed” is retained; “was killed” was a mistranslation. The speaker discrepancy remains open.

The saved whole Venice Terumot8 final-halakhah scalar has Zenobia speak, then an entering Saracen carrying a sword say that Bar Nitzor killed his brother. This confirms active killed rather than was killed but differs from Hyman’s assignment of the sword sentence to Zenobia. Source Ami and named Imi, and Netzer/Nitzor, remain distinct. The successful connected chapter-selector paragraph supersedes the earlier failed segment fetch, not proof of universal chapter absence. No modern historical identity or genealogy is admitted.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. I, p. 275) cites Ketubot 51a. Ketubot 51b includes the king-versus-bandit comparison, and Rashi there says Ben Netzer captured towns and ruled them. The printed sword clause uses קטיל, while the supplied transcription has קטל. In Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 8:4, Zenobia first addresses Rabbi Imi and Rabbi Shmuel. An entering Saracen then says Bar Nitzor killed his brother with the sword. Hyman assigns the shortened sword statement to Zenobia. The edition behind his attribution is unidentified. Bereshit Rabbah 76:6 identifies Ben Netzer with the small horn in its exposition of Daniel.
